//: Copy to <your-repo>/.claude/work.config.json and edit. Every key is OPTIONAL — the harness runs single-host, local-only, with no repo identity if this file is absent. Keys marked REQUIRED-FOR are only needed for the feature named.
//repo: REQUIRED-FOR cloud leads and the preflight identity check. These five values used to be hardcoded in work-runner.mjs; that is what made the harness un-shareable.
//repo.mergeMode: How the shepherd lands a PR (DER-2753). "queue" = arm the native GitHub merge queue with `gh pr merge <n> --auto` and let the queue own the strategy. "direct" = the shepherd merges itself with `gh pr merge <n> --<mergeStrategy> --delete-branch --match-head-commit <sha>` — for the MAJORITY of repos, which have no merge queue. OMIT the key to auto-detect once per `ready` call (GraphQL repository.mergeQueue on the default branch). If the probe cannot answer, the mode stays UNRESOLVED and NOTHING is merged — set it explicitly rather than let the harness guess. In direct mode the harness reproduces client-side the only protection the queue was giving you: it merges ONLY when `ready` passes every gate (not draft, 0 unresolved threads, Codex on head, checks pass, gate evidence current), and (DER-2774) it BINDS the printed command to the exact head those gates were evaluated against — `ready` prints a command you run later, so without --match-head-commit a push landing in between would merge a tree nothing gated. Run the command `ready` printed, verbatim; do not retype it without the pin.
//repo.mergeStrategy: direct mode only: "squash" (default) | "merge" | "rebase". Ignored in queue mode, where passing a strategy is a documented mistake.
//repo.allowMergeWithoutChecks: A LOOSENING — default false, leave it false if you have any CI. A repo with NO checks at all can never satisfy the checks gate, so `ready` would hold forever; set true to merge on the remaining gates (draft / threads / Codex-on-head / gate evidence) when there is genuinely no CI to wait for. It waives EXACTLY ONE answer — checks=ABSENT, meaning `gh pr checks` ran and reported no checks on the branch. fail, pending, and UNKNOWN (the probe itself could not be read — auth, throttle, timeout, no gh) ALL still block with this on. DER-2774: before that fix the waiver keyed on an unset value, which the probe also returned for a dead probe AND for a RED tree on any repo without a job literally named `checks` — so on most repos this key silently meant "ignore CI". The waiver is printed in the `ready` verdict and header and recorded on `run_started`, so it stays auditable. Needs gh >= 2.50.0, which added `pr checks --json` (cli/cli#9079); verified on 2.76.2 and 2.86.0.
//trustedCommentAuthors: SECURITY (DER-2737). PR comments are how a CLOUD lead reports lifecycle events (WORK-EVENT / WORK-HANDOFF), and the fold treats them as privileged ledger input — so it accepts them ONLY from these logins, plus `repo.ownerLogin` and known harness bots. Deny-by-default: with no `repo.ownerLogin` configured, NO human login is trusted and comment folding is off. Add a second maintainer or a bot that posts on the harness's behalf here. Anyone who can comment on any open PR in the repo can otherwise write your ledger.
//trustedPrAuthors: SECURITY (DER-2778). A SEPARATE list from `trustedCommentAuthors` — do not merge them. Cloud-lead lifecycle (`lead_online` / `handed_off`) is derived from OPEN PR STATE discovered with `gh pr list --state open --limit 100`, i.e. ANY open PR in the repo, and relevance used to be a branch-or-title SUBSTRING match on a run's issue id. On a PUBLIC repo whose PR titles carry issue ids, a fork PR titled with an in-flight id therefore retargeted a live unit's tracked PR and cleared its pending kickback. A PR is now read as this run's only when its AUTHOR is `repo.ownerLogin` or a login listed here, AND its head repository owner is the owner segment of `repo.repoSlug` (a fork never is). Deny-by-default: with no `repo` block configured, NO PR is trusted and cloud-lead discovery is off. `trustedCommentAuthors` deliberately includes the Codex review bot — its COMMENTS are authoritative input — but that bot is NOT a trusted PR author: a PR it opens is not one of your leads. Add here the login a cloud env's `GH_TOKEN` authors PRs as, when that is not `repo.ownerLogin`.
//commitAuthor: Commits are authored as this identity, and it is what reaches a CLOUD lead's brief as its `git config user.name/email` step (DER-2749). Some deploy checks (e.g. Vercel) map commit author → account and red the PR on a mismatch. BOTH keys are required together: a half-set identity is REFUSED when a cloud brief is written, because name-without-email would make the lead run `git config user.email ""` and actively set a broken author rather than leave the environment default alone. Omit the whole block if you do not care about commit identity — then no git-config step is emitted at all.
//hosts: Where leads run. `local` always exists. `kind:"ssh"` overflows to another machine over cmux ssh; `kind:"cloud"` is a Claude Code cloud environment spawned via the RemoteTrigger tool. One entry PER ACCOUNT — environmentId is per-account and credProfile pins which login it is spawned from.
//preferHosts: Default host order for every lead when the run sets no --host/--prefer. pickHost fills-then-spills across them.
//worktreeRoot: Where per-issue worktrees are created. Must be outside the repo.
//collision: How the harness decides two issues cannot run in parallel. versionHolder* name files whose concurrent edits pass git but fail a CI version guard; serializedFiles are files only one in-flight PR may touch; scopeKeySegments is how many path segments make a scope key.
//dockerScopePrefixes: Issues touching these paths need a Docker-capable host (real-database tests). Feeds the pickHost capability gate so such an issue is never spilled to a noDocker host.
//budget: Per-issue circuit breaker. A trip is a decision point (split / re-scope / park), not an auto-kill.
//shepherdModel: The shepherd's inline fixes merge with no second reviewer, so default it to your strongest model.
//leadTypes: OPTIONAL. Non-default lead models. `proxy:true` routes through a local gateway (localhost only); `provider` names a direct third-party endpoint. Tokens are NEVER stored here — the harness builds a runtime shell expression that reads them from your gateway config or repo env file at launch, so no key reaches a ledger event or a logged command line.
//modelPrices: OPTIONAL. USD per 1M tokens, for the cost column in `work-metrics`. Deliberately empty by default — a stale price table silently reports wrong money.
